# Auth and data foundation: Drizzle, Commands endpoint, jsonb content

Spec 4 makes state real: email+password auth and per-User persistence for Threads, Paper, and Apply. These are the load-bearing choices; supersede any of them only with a follow-up ADR.

**ORM: Drizzle.** `drizzle-orm` + `pg`, schema as plain TypeScript in `pgSchema("openpath_app")`, migrations generated by `drizzle-kit` and committed as SQL under `apps/api/drizzle/`. Chosen over Prisma because the api builds with plain `tsc` (no codegen step, no engine binary) and Better Auth ships a first-class Drizzle adapter. Migrations are applied by a compiled script via Railway's `preDeployCommand` — once per deploy, a failure aborts the rollout, and `GET /health` never touches the DB (the deploy healthcheck invariant stays under test).

**Transport: REST reads + one mutation door.** Queries are plain GETs. Every mutation — user click today, Coach tool call later — goes through `POST /api/commands/:name`, resolved by a single Command registry: name, zod input schema, authorization, `coachAllowed` flag, `destructive` (confirm-required) flag, reversal descriptor, real success/failure envelope. This is ADR-0003's parity rule made physical: there is no second write path for the Coach to drift onto. No tRPC — the registry already provides the one typed procedure layer, and the Coach calls over HTTP, not through a TS client. Shared zod schemas, DTOs, and codecs live in `@workspace/domain` (tsc-built so the api can resolve it at runtime).

**Paper content (settles PRODUCT.md open question 3).** `paper_docs` stores `content_kind` (`cv | letter | proof`) + `content jsonb` + `content_version int`. The prototype's `cv:v1:`/`proof:v1:` prefixed strings are retired — that was transport smuggled into storage. Letters are jsonb too (`{ "markdown": string }`): every doc is a kind, a version, and a document. Version bumps are explicit codec upgrades in `@workspace/domain`, never in-place mutation of stored rows.

**Auth: Better Auth on the Hono API.** Email+password only, cookie sessions, mounted at `/api/auth/*`. Cross-origin (web on Vercel, api on Railway): CORS `credentials: true`, `SameSite=None; Secure`, and `trustedOrigins` reusing the same single-`*` origin matcher as `WEB_ORIGINS` — one origin policy, not two. Env: `SESSION_SECRET`, `AUTH_URL`. Email verification is off; verify/reset links are logged until an email provider lands (follow-up ticket). Known caveat: Safari ITP dislikes `*.vercel.app` ↔ `*.railway.app` cookies; the durable fix is sibling custom domains (follow-up ticket, not on this spec's critical path).

**Row identity and ordering.** App tables use app-generated UUIDv7 (time-ordered, safe for future optimistic client generation); Better Auth keeps its own text ids, so `user_id` is `text`. Server owns `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz`; clients derive display strings. Apply kanban in-stage order is a fractional-index `position text` column — a move writes one row.

**Access and first-run.** The whole app is behind sign-in; only the sign-in/sign-up screens and `GET /health` are public. New accounts are seeded with neutral starter content (sample CV, a few Apply cards, one starter Thread) — never the demo persona. Pitch persistence is deferred; when it lands it is one jsonb document per user, same shape as Paper content.

**Out of scope here:** real Coach LLM (uses this registry when it arrives), OAuth/passkeys, email provider, Pitch persistence, offline/local-first sync.
